checks.comparison: This setup encodes the fixed square-root-tuned accuracy and time guarantee of source Theorem7, under the analytic assumptions, source large-sample condition and explicitly approved scheduling-independence departure. It returns one selected point and the literal run's actual finite clock. The visible success criterion is integrability plus expected squared-gradient norm <=epsilon and the displayed 12/192 expected-time inequality. The separate optimality comparison is not asserted by defining this setup. The eleven direct Params fields are d,m,n,Lminus,Lpm,Delta,epsilon,x0,tau,Lplus,lower. publicInput constructs Simple from only d,m,n,Lminus,Lpm,Delta,epsilon,x0: tau, lower and Lplus are hidden. There are no S,rho,eta,K or budget fields. The batch and probability depend only on m; the source-family step and accuracy horizon then depend on known smoothness/gap/accuracy parameters. No latency information is available to this factory. The time bound is exactly 12*t(m)+(192*Delta*max(Lminus,Lpm)/epsilon)*t(sqrt(m)), matching source Theorem7. The equilibrium argument is the unrounded real sqrt(m), embedded via ENNReal.ofReal, while the executed batch is its natural ceiling; the later proof must justify this distinction using the equilibrium comparison and rounding estimates. The real coefficient is nonnegative under valid. The clock is the lintegral of actual output.2, with no finite-expectation or clock-integrability premise; gradient integrability is separately stated for output.1. The source paragraph immediately after Theorem7 explicitly states that the time bound is true when m>=n*log n even when n>sqrt(m), while optimality is not guaranteed in that latter regime. Therefore valid correctly has m>=n*log n and no n<=sqrt(m) condition. The extra worker restriction and smoothness normalization belong to the separately preserved supporting optimality comparison, not this accuracy/time interface.
